title: Embrace constraints
coreMove: Read a real shortage as a design input rather than a stop sign; the limit forces the essential choices, so ask what to cut or simplify before asking for more.

exampleSpecs.audience: founders who equate more headcount with better output
exampleSpecs.stakes: hire up to match rivals or stay small and stay focused
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist treats a small team as focus rather than a deficiency

exampleSpecs.audience: makers who believe total freedom yields better work
exampleSpecs.stakes: demand a bigger budget or build inside the tight one
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist uses a creative limit to force sharper choices

exampleSpecs.audience: teams that inventory their shortages before starting
exampleSpecs.stakes: wait until the gaps are filled or start with what is on hand
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist stops treating a list of lacks as a precondition

exampleSpecs.audience: designers who assume more features mean more robustness
exampleSpecs.stakes: ship the feature-heavy build or strip it to the lean core
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: leanness makes a weak part visible and therefore fixable

exampleSpecs.audience: leaders tempted to romanticize every shortage
exampleSpecs.stakes: celebrate the deprivation or name the barrier that must be removed
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist distinguishes a creative limit from a real obstacle

exampleSpecs.audience: organizers whose first instinct is to request more budget
exampleSpecs.stakes: lead with a funding request or lead with design questions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist makes design thinking the first response to a limit
